answer: An insurer auctions one underwriting fee for each voyage leg, identified by a port-signed route from a knoll beacon to a zenith transit window. Agents lock collateral and quote the risk; the contract accepts one winning quote per leg, regardless of how many aliases submit it. To earn on ten legs, an attacker must fund ten exposures and pay claims when forecasts fail. A carrier and port could collude to invent legs, so independent arrival records and random audits are needed; even those cannot prove every operator is unrelated.
